claims.text: Large atomic-size mismatch produces local lattice distortion in equimolar high-entropy nanoalloys.
Lattice distortion increases the activation energy for atomic diffusion at elevated temperatures.
The increased diffusion activation energy decreases atomic mobility.
Distortion fields raise local potential-energy barriers for vacancy-mediated diffusion.
Distortion fields raise local potential-energy barriers for interstitial-mediated diffusion.
Decreased atomic mobility slows grain-boundary migration.
Decreased atomic mobility hinders the nucleation and growth of secondary phases.
Slower grain-boundary migration improves structural stability by suppressing grain growth.
Sluggish diffusion improves chemical stability by suppressing phase separation.
Replacing an alloying element with a significantly different-sized atom will produce more lattice distortion than replacing it with a similarly sized atom.
The high-distortion sample will exhibit at least 20% less average grain-size increase after annealing than the low-distortion baseline.
The high-distortion sample will have no more than 10% secondary-phase volume fraction after annealing.
The prediction applies to equimolar five-component nanoalloys with initial grain size below 100 nm annealed at 700–900 °C for no more than 100 h.
The prediction may not apply to coarse-grained or non-equimolar systems.
Quantitative activation-energy differences for the relevant specific compositions have not yet been reported.
